MCL strengthens E-Waste Management Across Its Establishments under Special Campaign 6
articles.full_content:
Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) has joined the nation in observing Special campaign 6 and is undertaking significant initiatives to promote responsible e-waste management across its Headquarters and operational areas. Special campaign 6 will be observed till 31 st October 2026 focusing on systematic waste collection, environmental awareness and promotion of cleanliness across all MCL establishments.
As part of the drive, e-waste collection kiosks are set up across MCL areas to facilitate the collection and responsible disposal of discarded electronic items through authorised recycling channels. Employees at the Headquarters and operational areas are enthusiastically participating in the campaign, contributing to cleanliness initiatives and promoting environmentally responsible practices.
Awareness activities are also being conducted to sensitise employees and nearby communities about the harmful effects of improper e-waste disposal, including soil and water contamination and associated risks to human health and the environment.
In the first week of implementation phase of the campaign, MCL cleaned 73 sites out of the 240 identified sites, cleaning an area of 3,06,663 sqft against the target area of 10,00,000 sqft. The campaign also targets the disposal of 600 metric tonnes of scrap, while 350 HEMM batteries have been disposed of generating revenue through scrap disposal.
Through Special Campaign 6, MCL is reinforcing its commitment to workplace cleanliness, environmental protection and responsible e-waste management supporting the national objective of a cleaner, more sustainable and resource-efficient future.
articles.summary: Mahanadi Coalfields Limited (MCL) has joined the nation in observing Special campaign 6 and is undertaking significant initiatives to promote responsible e-waste management across its Headquarters and operational areas. Special campaign 6 will be observed till 31 st October 2026 focusing on systematic waste collection, environmental awareness and promotion of cleanliness across all MCL establishments. As part of the drive, e-waste collection kiosks are set up across MCL areas to facilitate the collection and responsible disposal of discarded electronic items through authorised recycling channels.

Industrial Pollution Abatement: Sustainability through Regulations under Namami Gange
articles.full_content:
Industrial pollution abatement is emerging as a key pillar river rejuvenation, with regulation increasingly evolving from conventional enforcement to continuous compliances, scientific monitoring, cleaner production, resource efficiency and technological improvement.
Under Namami Gange Programme, industrial pollution control has been strengthened through systematic inventorisation and annual inspection of Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs), independent technical assessments, implementing sector-specific Charters, monitoring of Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs), targeted action plans and sustained regulatory follow-up. Together, these interventions are creating a more accountable and sustainable pathway for industries to reduce pollution while improving water and resource efficiency.
From periodic inspection to continuous compliance
A major intervention has been the establishment of an Annual Inspection mechanism for GPIs, which commenced in 2017 with support of CPCB, the National Regulatory Authority. The programme focusses on 100% inspection of GPIs in the Ganga basin, through third party agencies e.g., technical institutes of national importance and online submission of inspection reports through mobile applications/web portals to enhance efficacy and transparency. For the 2026 inspection cycle, 40 technical institutes have been nominated to participate in the inspection process.
The scale of this monitoring framework has expanded considerably since 2017. In the 2025 inspection cycle, 3,703 GPIs were assessed (1,296 GPIs in the Ganga basin and 2,407 GPIs in the Yamuna basin). The exercise covered 113 districts across six States and one Union Territory, with the GPIs having potential to discharge into 46 tributaries and sub-tributaries of the Ganga and Yamuna.
The inspections go beyond visual assessment. The prescribed methodology includes studying the compliance of the industries against ‘Consent to Operate’ issued by State regulators (State Pollution Control Board) to the individual Industries, sampling from ETP inlets, outlets and aeration tanks, assessment of flow, pH, BOD, COD, TSS and TDS, verification of OCEMS connectivity, examination of recipient drains and water bodies, groundwater assessment, checks for any bypasses and ZLD profiling wherever applicable. Cases involving bypasses, multiple discharge points or defunct/non-existent/non-operational ETPs/ GPIs are reported with geo-tagged photographic or videographic evidence in the portal itself.
Regulation delivering measurable results
The progressive assessment of GPIs demonstrates the impact of sustained regulatory intervention. Across the assessed GPIs, compliance increased from 39% in 2017 to 70% in 2025, while the number of operational GPIs stood at 3,154 in 2025 increasing from 888 in 2017. During the same period, BOD load declined from 26 TPD (2017) to 12.02 TPD (2025), reflecting a substantial reduction in pollution load.

Under Namami Gange Programme, industrial pollution control has been strengthened through systematic inventorisation and annual inspection of Grossly Polluting Industries (GPIs), independent technical assessments, implementing sector-specific Charters, monitoring of Common Effluent Treatment Plants (CETPs), targeted action plans and sustained regulatory follow-up. MLA Reasi Kuldeep Raj hails Make in India and Atmanirbhar Bharat; says technological developments and research have opened new avenues in the field of agriculture and medicine
articles.full_content:
On the second day of 8-day exhibition on "12 Years of Government" organised at Katra by Central Bureau of Communication, Sh Kuldeep Raj Dubey, MLA Reasi said that the country under the leadership of Prime Minister Sh Narendra Modi has reached unprecedented heights of progress across sectors. He said that transformative changes taking place in the country and in the region provide new opportunities to the youth to further scale new heights in their career and contribute to the PM's vision of Viksit Bhart 2047.
The 8 day multimedia exhibition organized by the Central Bureau of Communication (CBC), Jammu, Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Government of India on its second day focussed on rural development, agricultural innovation, healthcare, tuberculosis awareness, and anti-drug initiatives.
While elaborating on various developmental initiatives of the Government, Sh Kuldeep Raj stated that initiatives like Make in India are transforming the economy of the country while taking care of India's strategic interests. He cited India's swift indigenous vaccine development during the COVID-19 pandemic, strategic defense advancements like S-400 and BrahMos missile systems, and the engineering milestone of the Reasi Chenab Rail Arch Bridge as a testimony to the positive change brought by initiatives Make in India s Atmanirbhar Bharat. He said that science, technology, innovation and research were the cornerstones of Make in India initiative. He emphasized the need for instilling scientific temper among the students so that India would become atmanirbhar in various sectors.
While referring to Nasha Mukt Bharat abhiyan of Union government, Sh Kuldeep Raj stated various anti-drug measures, were taken by the UT administration including the Reasi administration under the 100 day anti drug campaign. He also mentioned that various initiatives were taken for urging students and youth to lean towards self-employment through central startup funding schemes.
While addressing the gathering, Sh. Kuldeep Raj lauded the efforts of the Central Bureau of Communication for hosting the 12-year developmental exhibition at the holy town of Mata Vaishno Devi, Katra, underlined the importance of such awareness initiatives for reaching out to the people in remote areas of J&K. He said that the holistic communication campaign will help in creating a positive change in people and will help in effective and accountable governance.
Earlier, while welcoming the gathering, Ms. Neha Jalali, Director, CBC and PIB Jammu, outlined the need for grassroots awareness along with new media as an effective communication strategy for reaching out to the grassroots level. She said that the exhibition organised by CBC was being conducted with active support of Reasi/Katra administration and various departments with synergy for the benefit of public.
Ms Jalali urged the youth to use new and digital media for active engagement with the government and for making it a medium of positive change i

Ministry of MSME Concludes ‘Swachhata Hi Seva 2026’ Campaign with Nationwide Cleanliness and Awareness Initiatives
articles.full_content:
Union Minister for MSME Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi Leads Cleanliness Drive as Ministry of MSME Promotes Jan Bhagidari and Environmental Sustainability under Swachhata Hi Seva 2026
The Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) observed Swachhata Hi Seva (SHS) 2026 from 17 th September to 2 nd October 2026, culminating in Swachh Bharat Diwas on 2 October 2026. Guided by the theme “Swachhata Mein Sahbhag, Swachh Bharat, Viksit Bharat”, the campaign focused on promoting cleanliness, environmental sustainability and Jan Bhagidari across the Ministry, its attached offices and autonomous bodies.
As part of the campaign, Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Minister for MSME; Shri Bharat Khera, Secretary, Ministry of MSME; and Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME), participated in a cleanliness drive at MSME-DFO, Bal Sahyog, Connaught Place, under the ‘Ek Din, Ek Ghanta, Ek Saath’ initiative on 1 st October 2026. More than 150 participants participated in the cleanliness drive, underscoring the importance of collective action in maintaining clean public spaces. Tree plantation activities were also undertaken under the ‘Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam’ initiative, reinforcing the Ministry’s commitment to environmental conservation and sustainable development.
The campaign commenced with the administration of the Swachhata Pledge by Dr. Rajneesh, Additional Secretary & Development Commissioner (MSME). Approximately 250 officials of the Ministry of MSME and its field offices participated in the pledge and reaffirmed their commitment to cleanliness and the vision of Swachh Bharat.
As part of awareness and sensitisation activities, the Ministry sensitised officers and representatives of its attached offices, autonomous bodies and field formations on the objectives and significance of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026. The campaign encouraged participating organisations to undertake meaningful cleanliness drives, awareness programmes and sustainable initiatives in their offices and surrounding areas.
During the campaign period, the Ministry and its field formations across the country undertook activities under key components including CTU (Cleanliness Target Unit) Transformation & Clean Public Places, Swachh Paathshala, SafaiMitra Suraksha Evam Samman Shivir, Jan Bhagidari for Swachhata, and Swachhata se Samriddhi. These initiatives helped strengthen public participation, promote awareness on cleanliness and reinforce the importance of sustainable and collective efforts towards a Swachh Bharat.
